answer: SybilRank-style random-walk trust propagation: a few verified seeds release many short walks across the interaction graph. Honest agents live in a dense region, so walks keep landing on them, while Sybil clusters attach through only a few narrow bridges, like one opal thread tying a counterfeit haven to the real town. Each score is its share of landings, so a thousand fakes behind one bridge split a single thin stream of trust. To gain weight, an attacker must earn genuine links from agents, and every voyage into the honest region costs relationships, not just compute.
